title: Reverse Engineering the Dynamics of UFOs: A Physics-Based Assessment of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena
description:
A source-critical physics assessment of reported UFO/UAP flight characteristics. The paper compares the public evidence behind the "Five Observables" with candidate mechanisms including Alcubierre warp metrics, nuclear fusion, quantum-field effects, and metamaterials.

The analysis distinguishes calibrated measurements from witness-dependent or model-dependent estimates. Public UAP data do not presently establish the extreme kinematics used in many propulsion arguments, and a mathematically valid metric is not evidence that its required stress-energy distribution can be physically realized, formed, stabilized, or controlled.

The assessment cross-references 71 bibliography sources (42 peer-reviewed, 9 government, 12 DIRDs, 7 books, and 1 preprint). Government documents are treated as primary sources for institutional facts, not as independent validation of physical mechanisms; DIRDs are treated as commissioned technical analyses rather than peer-reviewed evidence.

AI Collaboration: Produced in structured collaboration with Claude (Anthropic), Codex, and GPT-5.4. AI systems assisted literature synthesis, structure, translation, repository validation, and consistency checks. All scientific judgments, assessments, and conclusions are solely those of the human author.

Data Verification: 42 of 45 quantitative records are marked as source-cross-checked in repository metadata. This indicates provenance review, not independent empirical confirmation; two model-dependent estimates are retained as low-confidence analysis and one withdrawn derived ratio is retained as a "not defined" record. Full audit details are provided in the accompanying verification reports.

Bilingual: English and Traditional Chinese (繁體中文).
notes: Version 1.2.7. UNCLASSIFIED — Open Source Analysis. Bilingual (English / Traditional Chinese). AI-assisted (Claude Opus 4 / Claude Sonnet 4, Anthropic; Codex; GPT-5.4); all scientific conclusions by human author.
